ἐνδυναμοῦται ὑπὸ τῆς παναλκοῦς καὶ πανδυνάμου θεϊκῆς ἰσχύος, οὐκ ἐνδυναμοῖ δὲ αὐτή.τὴν γὰρ αὐτῇ διαρκοῦσαν ἐδέξατο δύναμιν, καὶ μεταδιδόναι τοῖς συνδούλοις οὐ σθένει. τὸ δέ γε πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ γονίμῳ καὶ θρεπτικῇ καὶ ἀνεκλείπτῳ αὐτοῦ ἰσχύι ἐνδυναμοῖ, ἐπειδὴ κτίστης καὶ οὐ κτίσμα τυγχάνει. ὁ γὰρ σωτὴρ ἐν ταῖς πράξεσι φησίν· «ὑμεῖς δὲ λήψεσθε δύναμιν, ἐπελθόντος τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐφ' ὑμᾶς.» ὡς δίχα τῆς αὐτοῦ ἐπιφοιτήσεως οὐδεμίας ἡμῖν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν δυνάμεως ἢ ἐλπίδος ὑπαρχούσης. κατανοητέον δὲ πρὸς τούτῳ, ἓν μὲν, ὅτι τὴν παρουσίαν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος κατ' ἐξουσίαν σημαίνει γεγενῆσθαι· ἕτερον δέ, ὅτι οὐκ αὐτάγγελος ἦλθεν, ἀλλ' ὑπ' αὐτοῦ τοῦ μεγάλου θεοῦ καὶ σωτῆρος προεμηνύθη. καὶ αὖθις οὖν λέγει· «ὑμεῖς δὲ καθίσατε ἐν τῇ πόλει, ἕως οὗ ἐνδύσησθε δύναμιν ἐξ ὕψους.» αὕτη δὲ ἦν ἡ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος. καὶ Παῦλος γράφει Ῥωμαίοις, ἃ θαυμάσαι ἢ ἑρμηνεῦσαι ἀξίως, μάλιστα ἐξ ἐπιδρομῆς, οὐδενὶ εὐπετές· «ἔχω οὖν πεποίθησιν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ πρὸς τὸν θεόν. οὐ γὰρ τολμῶ τι λαλεῖν, ὧν οὐ κατειργάσατο Χριστὸς δι' ἐμοῦ λόγῳ καὶ ἔργῳ εἰς ὑπακοὴν ἐθνῶν, ἐν δυνάμει σημείων καὶ τεράτων ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος ἁγίου.» 6.13ν ὅτι ἀψευδές· ὅπερ ἴδιον μόνου θεοῦ ἡ κτίσις οὐκ ἀληθεύει ἀεί, ἀλλ' ἐξ οἰκείας γνώμης ἔχει τροπῆς μέρος καὶ τὸ ψεύδεσθαί ποτε. ὡς ἐν μὲν ἀσάρκοις ὁ διάβολος, ἐν δὲ σαρκίνοις καθὰ γράφει· «πᾶς ἄνθρωπος ψεύστης,» καί· «ἀπολεῖς πάντας τοὺς λαλοῦντας τὸ ψεῦδος.» οὐ γὰρ ἐπιψεύδεσσι πατὴρ θεὸς ἔσσετ' ἀρωγός, ἔγραψαν καὶ οἱ ἔξω. ἐν δὲ ἁγίοις, ὡς Παῦλος περὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἔφη· «ἀλλ' ὅτε εἶδον, ὅτι οὐκ ὀρθοποδοῦσιν πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ εὐαγ γελίου, εἶπον τῷ Κηφᾷ ἔμπροσθεν πάντων» ἃ εἶπεν. ὡς ἀληθῶς γὰρ μόνης θεϊκῆς φύσεως τὸ ἀεὶ ἀψευδεῖν. διὸ Ἑβραίοις ἐπέστειλεν· «ἵνα» φησίν, «διὰ δύο πραγμάτων ἀμεταθέτων, ἐν οἷς ἀδύνατον ψεύ σασθαι τὸν θεόν, ἰσχυρὰν παράκλησιν ἔχωμεν οἱ καταφυγόντες κρατῆ σαι τῆς προκειμένης ἐλπίδος.» ἡ δὲ κοινωνία τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, κοινωνοῦσα τῇ φύσει τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ, κοινωνεῖ εἰς ὅλα, ἔτι μὴν καὶ εἰς τὸ ἀψευδεῖν. πνεῦμα γὰρ ἀληθείας ἐστὶν τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς προελέχθη, τῷ ἑνὶ θελήματι τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ καὶ ἑαυτοῦ λαλοῦν, καὶ ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ οὐ λαλοῦν, ὡς ὁ υἱὸς αὐτῷ ἐμαρτύρησεν εἰπών· «ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ οὐ λαλήσει.» 6.14ν ὅτι ἀλήθεια, διὰ τὸ μὴ διαφωνεῖν αὐτὸ πρὸς τὴν μίαν θεότητα. ἡ κτίσις οὐδὲν ἔχει προσαγορευθὲν ἀλήθεια, διὰ τὸ μίαν εἶναι θεϊκὴν ἀλήθειαν, ὡς μία ἐστὶν ἡ ἁγιότης καὶ ἡ ἀγαθότης, ἀφ' ἧς ἑκάστοις ἡμῖν ταῦτα 63 ἐφήκειν ὁμολογοῦμεν. τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἀλήθεια προσηγόρευται καθὰ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ὁ υἱός, ἐπειδὴ τῆς αὐτῆς μιᾶς ἐστιν θεότητος, οὐδὲν ἔχον πολυσχιδὲς ἢ διαφωνοῦν. μαρτυρεῖ δὲ περὶ μὲν τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ ἑαυτοῦ ὁ υἱὸς λέγων· «πάτερ, ὁ λόγος ὁ σὸς ἀλήθειά ἐστιν,» καὶ πάλιν· «ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ζωὴ καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια,» περὶ δὲ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, ὡς προελέχθη. 6.15ν ὅτι οὐδεὶς οἶδεν τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰ μὴ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, καὶ ὅτι διὰ τὴν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἰσότητα, τὸ ἀνάπαλιν ὁ θεὸς οἶδεν τὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος. ἡ κτίσις οὐκ οἶδεν τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ· ὑπερβαίνει γὰρ αὐτήν, καὶ οὐδὲν πρὸς τοιαύτην εἴδησιν ὁρμῆσαι τολμᾷ, κἂν ᾖ τῶν εὐδοκίμων· ἐπειδὴ γνῶναι τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς πάμπαν ἀδύνατον τῇ μὴ οὔσῃ τῆς αὐτῆς φύσεως καὶ τὴν αὐτὴν γνῶσιν τῷ θεῷ κεκτημένῃ, ὡς ἐδίδαξεν ὁ σωτὴρ εἰπὼν ἐν Ἰωάννῃ· «ὁ δοῦλος οὐκ οἶδεν τί ποιεῖ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ,» καὶ ὡς ἔγραψεν Πέτρος· «ἔστιν ἃ νῦν ἀναγγέλλει ὑμῖν διὰ τῶν εὐαγγελισαμένων ὑμᾶς πνεύματι ἁγίῳ ἀποσταλέντι ἀπὸ οὐρανοῦ, εἰς ἃ ἐπιθυμοῦσιν ἄγγελοι παρακῦψαι.» τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ὅτι ἐπίσταται ὡς ὁμοούσιος θεός, ὁ ἀπόστολος Κορινθίοις ἐπέστειλεν, ὡς προείρηται. καὶ πάλιν τὴν μεγαλειότητα τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ τὴν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἰσότητα παριστῶν, ἰσόρροπον ἐκείνῳ γράφει· «ὁ δὲ ἐρευνῶν τὰς καρδίας οἶδεν, τί τὸ φρόνημα τοῦ πνεύματος.» καθὰ γὰρ μέγα τι λέγων περὶ τοῦ πατρὸς, εἶπεν εἰδέναι αὐτὸν τοῦ πνεύματος τὸ φρόνημα, οὕτω τὴν πρὸς αὐτὸν κοινωνίαν τῆς φύσεως καὶ θελήσεως καὶ τὴν But the Holy Spirit of God gives commands to prophets and apostles with his own authority, as God and Master, as may be shown in the chapters set out below. 6.12ν [Chapter title:] That it empowers. The creation is empowered by the all-strong and all-powerful divine might, but it does not itself empower. For it received the power that suffices for itself, and it has no strength to impart it to its fellow slaves. But the Spirit of God empowers by his fruitful and nourishing and unfailing might, since he is creator and not creature. For the Saviour says in the Acts: 'But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you,' since without his coming there is for us no power or hope toward God. And one must observe in addition to this, one thing, that he signifies that the presence of the Holy Spirit took place with authority; and another, that he did not come as his own messenger, but was announced beforehand by the great God and Saviour himself. And so again he says: 'But you, sit in the city until you are clothed with power from on high.' And this was the power of the Holy Spirit. And Paul writes to the Romans things which it is easy for no one to admire or to interpret worthily, least of all in passing: 'I have, then, confidence in Christ Jesus toward God. For I do not dare to speak of anything except what Christ worked through me, by word and deed, for the obedience of the Gentiles, in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Spirit.' 6.13ν [Chapter title:] That it is free from lying, which is proper to God alone. The creation does not always speak truly, but from its own will it has, as a part of its changeableness, also lying at times. As among the bodiless the devil; and among those in flesh, as it writes: 'Every man is a liar,' and: 'You will destroy all who speak falsehood.' 'For Father God will be no helper to liars,' even those outside wrote. And among the saints, as Paul said about the apostles: 'But when I saw that they were not walking straight toward the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before them all' what he said. For truly, always to be free from lying belongs to the divine nature alone. Therefore he wrote to the Hebrews: 'so that,' he says, 'through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge may have strong encouragement to lay hold of the hope set before us.' But the communion of the Holy Spirit, sharing in nature with the Father and the Son, shares in all things, and moreover also in being free from lying. For he is the Spirit of truth of God, as was said before, speaking by the one will of the Father and the Son and himself, and not speaking from himself, as the Son testified to him, saying: 'He will not speak from himself.' 6.14ν [Chapter title:] That it is truth, because it is not out of accord with the one Godhead. The creation has nothing that has been called 'truth', because the divine truth is one, as holiness and goodness are one, from which we confess that these things [printed line number 63, page debris] have come to each of us. But the Holy Spirit has been called 'truth', as the Father and the Son are, since he is of the same one Godhead, having nothing split into many parts or out of accord. And the Son bears witness about the Father and himself, saying: 'Father, your word is truth,' and again: 'I am the life and the truth'; and about the Holy Spirit, as was said before. 6.15ν [Chapter title:] That no one knows the things of God except the Holy Spirit; and that, because of his equality with the Father, conversely God knows the things of the Holy Spirit. The creation does not know the things of God; for they surpass it, and nothing dares to set out toward such knowledge, even if it be among those held in honour; since to know the things of God is altogether impossible for what is not of the same nature and does not possess the same knowledge as God, as the Saviour taught, saying in John: 'The slave does not know what his lord is doing,' and as Peter wrote: 'There are things which he now announces to you through those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, into which angels long to stoop and look.' But that the Holy Spirit knows, as consubstantial God, the apostle wrote to the Corinthians, as was said before. And again, setting forth the majesty of the Spirit and his equality with the Father, he writes something of equal weight to that: 'And he who searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit.' For just as, saying something great about the Father, he said that he knows the mind of the Spirit, so, setting forth the Holy Spirit's communion with him in nature and will and the equality of dignity and power, he wrote that he alone knows the things of the Father and searches his depths and his unknown thoughts, which one must also [the sentence continues in the next section].
pass_b_english: “…of his” (Psalm 103:20). But the Holy Spirit of God gives commands to prophets and apostles on his own authority, as God and Master, as may be shown in the chapters below.

Creation is empowered by the all-strong and all-powerful might of God, but it does not empower. It received only the power that suffices for itself, and it has no strength to share it with its fellow slaves. But the Spirit of God empowers by his fruitful, nourishing and unfailing might, since he is Creator and not creature. For the Saviour says in the Acts, “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you” (Acts 1:8), for without his coming we have no power or hope toward God.

Two further things should be noticed here. First, the Saviour shows that the Holy Spirit came with authority. Second, the Spirit did not come as his own messenger; he was announced beforehand by the great God and Saviour himself. So again he says, “But you, stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high” (Luke 24:49). And this was the power of the Holy Spirit.

Paul writes to the Romans words that no one can easily admire or explain as they deserve, least of all in passing: “I have, then, confidence in Christ Jesus toward God. For I will not dare to speak of anything except what Christ has worked through me, in word and deed, to bring the Gentiles to obedience, in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Spirit” (Romans 15:17-19).
That he does not lie, which is proper to God alone.

Creation does not always speak the truth. Of its own will, as one side of its changeableness, it sometimes lies too. Among the bodiless powers the devil does; among those in the flesh, as Scripture says, “Every man is a liar” (Psalm 116:11), and, “You will destroy all who speak falsehood” (Psalm 5:6). Even those outside the Church wrote, “Father God will be no helper to liars.” And so among the saints: Paul says of the apostles, “But when I saw that they were not walking straight according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before them all” (Galatians 2:14) what he said. Truly, never to lie belongs to the divine nature alone. That is why he wrote to the Hebrews, “so that,” he says, “through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled for refuge may have strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before us” (Hebrews 6:18).

But the Holy Spirit’s communion with the Father and the Son is a communion in nature, so it extends to all things, and so also to never lying. For he is the Spirit of truth of God, as was said before. He speaks by the one will of the Father and the Son and himself, and does not speak from himself, as the Son bore witness of him: “He will not speak on his own” (John 16:13).
That he is truth, because he is in full accord with the one Godhead.

Nothing in creation has been called “truth,” because the divine truth is one, just as holiness and goodness are one; and from that one source, we confess, these gifts have come to each of us. But the Holy Spirit has been called “truth,” as the Father and the Son are, since he belongs to the same one Godhead and has nothing in him split into many parts or out of accord. The Son bears witness about the Father and himself when he says, “Father, your word is truth” (John 17:17), and again, “I am the life and the truth” (John 14:6); and about the Holy Spirit, as was said before.
That no one knows the things of God except the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 2:11); and that, because the Spirit is equal to the Father, God in turn knows the things of the Holy Spirit.

Creation does not know the things of God. They surpass it, and no creature dares to set out after such knowledge, however highly it is esteemed. To know the things of God is altogether impossible for one who is not of God’s nature and does not have the same knowledge as God. So the Saviour taught, saying in John, “The slave does not know what his lord is doing” (John 15:15); and Peter wrote, “There are things which he now announces to you through those who preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven, things into which angels long to look” (1 Peter 1:12).

But that the Holy Spirit knows, as God of one substance with the Father, the apostle wrote to the Corinthians, as was said before. And again, setting forth the Spirit’s majesty and his equality with the Father, he writes a saying of equal weight: “And he who searches the hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit” (Romans 8:27). Saying something great about the Father, he said that the Father knows the mind of the Spirit. In the same way, setting forth the Holy Spirit’s communion with him in nature and will, and his equality in dignity and power, he wrote that the Spirit alone knows the things of the Father and searches his depths (1 Corinthians 2:10-11) and his unknown thoughts, which one must also…

choices.issue: Garbled machine draft with reversed claims, wrong references, chapter titles run into the text
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u15): retranslated from the Greek. The reader report (acts/SOURCE_ISSUES.md) flagged '(Luke 24:49/1:8)': the quotation 'stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high' is Luke 24:49 alone; Acts 1:8 is cited at its own quotation earlier. Other wrong references: (Romans 15:18) -> 15:17-19; 'Father, your word is truth' (John 1:14) -> John 17:17; (John 14:17) removed from 'Spirit of truth'. The old English also said creation 'does not fail to impart' power (the Greek says it has no strength to), put the coming chapters as 'the preceding chapters', made Homer's line into 'Father God will not lie', made the Romans preface into 'especially from an attack, not nothing pleasant', ran the chapter titles 6.12-6.15 into the text, and split 6.13's sentence across two paragraphs. Brackets [this], [he], [the power], [it is], [beings] removed; Psalm 103:20, 1 Corinthians 2:11 and 2:10-11 added.

choices.why: The section opens with the last word of the quotation of Psalm 103:20 (Greek 102:20) begun in the previous section ('doing the word…'); only that word is translated.
Each chapter title becomes its own paragraph without the number. The title of 6.15 alludes to 1 Corinthians 2:11 and carries that reference.

choices.term: καθὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑποκειμένοις κεφαλαίοις ἀποδειχθείη
choices.english: as may be shown in the chapters below
choices.why: ὑποκειμένοις points forward (to 6.12 and after); the optative is a modest 'may be shown'.

choices.english: It received only the power that suffices for itself
choices.why: 'only' brings out the contrast Didymus draws with the next clause (it cannot share it); it adds no claim.
The subject of σημαίνει is the Saviour speaking in Acts 1:8; named in English for clarity.

choices.english: the Spirit did not come as his own messenger
choices.why: αὐτάγγελος: one who brings his own news; the Spirit's coming was foretold by Christ, not self-announced.

choices.term: ὑπ' αὐτοῦ τοῦ μεγάλου θεοῦ καὶ σωτῆρος
choices.english: by the great God and Saviour himself
choices.why: A title of Christ from Titus 2:13; listed as a possible allusion, not cited inline.
Didymus has πεποίθησιν ('confidence') where the New Testament has καύχησιν ('ground for boasting'); his word is translated.

choices.term: οὐ γὰρ ἐπιψεύδεσσι πατὴρ θεὸς ἔσσετ' ἀρωγός
choices.english: “Father God will be no helper to liars.”
choices.why: Homer, Iliad 4.235 (οὐ γὰρ ἐπὶ ψευδέσσι πατὴρ Ζεὺς ἔσσετ' ἀρωγός), quoted by 'those outside' with θεός for Ζεύς. Translated as Didymus gives it; not Scripture, so no inline reference.
Pagan writers, as in u15-rem-early; 'the Church' added so the phrase is understood.

choices.english: Among the bodiless powers the devil does
choices.why: The elliptical Greek ('as among the bodiless, the devil') is completed with 'does' (lies).

choices.term: ἡ δὲ κοινωνία τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, κοινωνοῦσα τῇ φύσει
choices.english: the Holy Spirit’s communion with the Father and the Son is a communion in nature, so it extends to all things
choices.why: The participle is turned into a main clause so the chain (communion in nature, therefore in everything, therefore in truthfulness) reads aloud.

choices.term: ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ζωὴ καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια
choices.english: “I am the life and the truth” (John 14:6)
choices.why: Didymus abridges John 14:6 ('the way, the truth and the life') and reverses the order; his wording is kept.

choices.english: these gifts have come to each of us
choices.why: 63 is a printed line number, page debris; skipped. ταῦτα (holiness, goodness, truth) rendered 'these gifts'.

choices.english: There are things which he now announces to you
choices.why: Didymus' wording differs from the New Testament (ἃ νῦν ἀνηγγέλη, 'which have now been announced'); his active form is translated.

choices.english: as God of one substance with the Father
choices.why: ὁμοούσιος names the Father implicitly; 'with the Father' is added for English sense and matches the following sentence.
The sentence runs on into the next unit; the English ends with an ellipsis.
